rules.label: A parent with sole custody may act alone.

law_references.quote: A parent represents his or her child alone if: 1) he or she has sole legal custody of the child, or 2) the powers of decision have been transferred to him or her pursuant to § 119 of this Act.
law_references.note: This is the first explicit single-parent basis.

rules.label: A parent with delegated decision right may act alone.

law_references.quote: A parent represents his or her child alone if: 1) he or she has sole legal custody of the child, or 2) the powers of decision have been transferred to him or her pursuant to § 119 of this Act.
law_references.note: This is the second explicit single-parent basis.

rules.label: A parent may act alone in an emergency.

law_references.quote: If making a joint declaration of intention of the parents would cause a delay in conflict with the interests of the child, one parent has the right to enter into necessary transactions and perform necessary acts in the interests of the child also alone.
law_references.note: The urgent scenario is the user-facing demonstration rule.

rules.label: A parent may act with both parents' consent.

law_references.quote: Parents shall exercise joint legal custody with respect to their child and perform the custodial obligation on their own responsibility and unanimously considering all-round well-being of the child. Parents who have joint legal custody have a joint right of representation.
law_references.note: This captures the joint representation baseline.

rules.label: If one parent is unreachable, confirmed joint consent is unavailable.

law_references.quote: If making a joint declaration of intention of the parents would cause a delay in conflict with the interests of the child, one parent has the right to enter into necessary transactions and perform necessary acts in the interests of the child also alone.
law_references.note: A small demo simplification used to keep the trace readable.

rules.label: A non-parent cannot give the permission.

law_references.quote: A parent who has legal custody is the legal representative of a child. Parents who have joint legal custody have a joint right of representation.
law_references.note: This guards the demo against third-party requests.
